test_title: SSC CGL Tier-II 2023 Official Paper-I (Held On: 26 Oct, 2023)
subject: general
question: Which of the following is a possible criticism of privatisation?

options.text: Expansion of bureaucracy and efficiency in public enterprises
Excessive government interference into private businesses
Limited access to essential services for marginalised populations
Reduced competition and innovation in the market

solution:
The correct answer is **Limited access to essential services for marginalised populations**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Equity Issues**: Privatisation can lead to inequitable access to essential services, as private entities may prioritize profit over service provision to marginalized groups.
 
• **Service Costs**: Private companies may increase the cost of services, making them less affordable for low-income populations.
 
• **Quality of Service**: There is a risk that private companies may cut corners in service quality to maximize profits.
 
• **Accountability**: Public accountability might decrease, as private companies are not subject to the same level of scrutiny as public entities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 Aspect
 Description
 
 
 
 

 **Privatisation**
 The transfer of ownership, property, or business from the government to the private sector.
 
 

 **Public Services**
 Services provided by the government to its citizens, either directly or through financing private provision of services.
 
 

 **Market Efficiency**
 The extent to which market prices reflect all available, relevant information.
 
 

 **Profit Motive**
 The intent to achieve monetary gain in a transaction or material endeavor.
 
 

 **Regulation**
 Rules or directives made and maintained by an authority to regulate private sector activities.
